summary: Unwind assistance: deconstruct mixed batching + kv-cache + 8-bit quant profile causing higher tail latency and inference variance
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a pronounced increase in 95th/99th percentile latency and occasional semantic drift in outputs after enabling a combined optimizer profile: async batching (aggressive), KV prefix caching, and an 8-bit quantization profile pinned to their blue release. The change was applied via the tenant optimizer endpoint at 2026-03-09T14:03Z.

Impact:
- Affected ~7 routes used by NovaHealth conversational triage (avg traffic 2.1k rps).
- 95p latency increased from ~120ms to 420ms for long-session workloads; 99p spikes >900ms observed.
- Small but reproducible hallucination-like deviations on medical triage prompts (customer flagged 0.8% of cases).

Environment:
- prod-us-east, Dedicated cluster redwood-ded-nyc-03
- Model variants: redwood-open-7b (fp16) fallback, redwood-instruct-7b-8bit (quant) active
- Optimizer profile: tenant-nova-v3 (batching: async aggressive, kv_cache: enabled, quant_profile: 8bit-fast)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use customer route nova-triage-v1 with long conversation (>512 tokens cumulative).
2) Send 1:1 simulated traffic at 80% of normal (1.6k rps) with a mix of short and long sequences.
3) Observe latency distribution and sampled outputs.

Observed behavior:
- Elevated tail latency on long-session requests; CPU/GPU utilization patterns show increased scheduling jitter and queueing.
- KV cache hit rates dropped intermittently for a subset of sessions (suspected cache fragmentation).
- Quantized path returns slightly different logits for specific tokens leading to variance in deterministic prompts.

Expected behavior:
- Minimal change to 95/99p latency after conservative optimizer enablement and no semantic regressions beyond expected quantization noise.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: aggressive async batching increased inter-request scheduling that, combined with uneven prefix cache distribution and 8-bit quantized execution, caused hot-host skew and queueing leading to tail latency. Secondary hypothesis: the quantization microkernel for long sequences introduces small token probability perturbations that, combined with caching mismatches, expose semantic variance.

What we checked:
- Verified optimizer assignment timestamp and tenant-level gating (confirmed).
- Correlated host-level queue depth with optimizer enable time; three hosts show persistent queue amplification.
- KV cache telemetry: session affinity lost intermittently for long-lived websocket sessions (likely due to batching coalescing across connectors).
- Compared logits across fp16 and 8bit for sampled prompts: token-by-token diffs concentrated in punctuation and domain-specific terms (medical).

Evidence links:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serve/novahealth-tail-latency?orgId=1
- KV cache telemetry: https://internal.telemetry/nova/kvcache/tenant-nova-v3
actions_taken:
1) Placed temporary traffic gate to limit async batch size per-worker to 8 for nova-triage-v1 at 2026-03-10T10:00Z (partial mitigation).
2) Manually rebalanced traffic away from hosts gpu-45/gpu-46 to reduce hot-host queueing (drain + reassign).
3) Ran a local re-run comparing fp16 vs 8bit for 200 sampled prompts; captured token-level diffs.
4) Prepared a stepwise unwind plan (see recommended rollback below) and requested SRE approval for live snapshot restore if needed.
recommended_unwind_plan:
(safe, staged, per-route)
- Step 0: Create snapshot of current optimizer state and tenant config (done at 2026-03-10T10:05Z).
- Step 1: Reduce async batch max_size to 4 for nova-triage-v1 and monitor 95p/99p (30m).
- Step 2: If 95p not reduced, disable async batching (switch to sync batching with small max latency) for nova-triage-v1 and maintain kv_cache enabled (30m).
- Step 3: If variance persists, toggle kv_cache to read-only (no new entries) to check if eviction/access pattern is root cause (30m).
- Step 4: If accuracy drift remains correlated only with quant path, roll back quant_profile to fp16 for nova-triage-v1 (cold rollback of model variant to redwood-open-7b) and route a small shadow traffic split (5%) for validation before full cutover.
- Safety notes: perform changes one route at a time and wait 30m after each step before proceeding. Keep snapshot rollback path ready.

resolution: Work in progress. Short-term mitigation: batch size limit reduced and host rebalancing restored most of the 95p performance. Next steps agreed: disable aggressive async batching per-route and evaluate kv_cache read-only toggles before changing quant_profile. If quant path remains implicated, follow the staged model rollback to fp16 with a 5% shadow validation prior to full cutover. Customer (NovaHealth) has approved Step 1 and deferred Step 4 until after clinical sync. Follow-up ticket will capture final rollback and any post-change validation artifacts.
next_steps:
1) Execute Step 2 (disable async batching) for nova-triage-v1 in the next low-traffic window and capture 95/99p plus sampled outputs.
2) If 99p still elevated, toggle kv_cache to read-only to measure eviction impact.
3) If accuracy drift persists and metrics correlate with quant path, schedule Step 4 rollback to fp16 with 5% shadow traffic and run customer QA suite (pass threshold: no more than 0.2% semantic deviation on clinical prompts).
4) Document final changes and attach snapshot IDs and Grafana/telemetry links into the ticket before closing.
customer_communication: We informed NovaHealth about staged unwind and got approval for conservative steps. Asked to postpone any full quant rollback until after their clinical review on 2026-03-12. Committed to hourly updates during any active rollback window.
internal_notes: Consider adding a safety guard in optimizer rollout UI to limit simultaneous enabling of: (1) aggressive async batching, (2) kv cache writes, and (3) 8bit quant profiles for tenants with long-session conversational workloads. File a follow-up internal support task to propose guard UX: INT-204912.
